title: CVE-2026-87861: cross-origin reuse of a Negotiate connection
excerpt:
## Summary:
I found a cross-origin connection reuse flaw in `lib/url.c`, introduced by [bd10924b4](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/bd10924b4) as part of the recently announced "Patch the Planet" initiative. It causes a request for one origin to be sent on a connection that was authenticated with Negotiate for a different origin, while the requesting transfer's own credentials go unused.

My research looked at the reuse matchers that [bd10924b4](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/bd10924b4) rewrote. The commit closed [#22040](https://github.com/curl/curl/pull/22040) by adding `conn->creds_origin` and comparing it against `data->state.origin`. This activity is correct, but the issue is in the branch the commit replaced. At the parent [c2b050e4e496](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/c2b050e4e496), the credential mismatch branch of `url_match_auth_ntlm` recorded a connection as a reuse candidate only when both auth states were idle:

```c
#ifdef USE_SPNEGO
      if((conn->http_ntlm_state == NTLMSTATE_NONE) &&
         (conn->http_negotiate_state == GSS_AUTHNONE)) {
#else
      if(conn->http_ntlm_state == NTLMSTATE_NONE) {
#endif
        m->found = conn;
      }
```

[bd10924b4](https://github.com/curl/curl/commit/bd10924b4) replaced that entire branch with a single early return gated on `conn->creds`, so the `GSS_AUTHNONE` condition is gone. That gate does not fire in the ordinary Kerberos SSO case. `Curl_http_output_auth` exempts Negotiate from the no-credentials early out, so `--negotiate` with no `-u` runs from the ticket cache with `data->state.creds` `NULL`, and `Curl_input_negotiate` links `conn->creds_origin` to the origin while `Curl_creds_link(&conn->creds, NULL)` leaves `conn->creds` `NULL`. A later transfer whose wanted auth includes `NTLM` (`CURLAUTH_ANY` masks off only `CURLAUTH_DIGEST_IE` and `CURLAUTH_HTTPSIG`, so `--anyauth` qualifies) then passes `url_match_auth`, because `needle->creds` is `NULL` for HTTP and `Curl_creds_same(NULL, NULL)` is `TRUE`. 

It reaches the state-NONE branch at `url.c:937`, where the origin comparison is gated on `conn->creds` and does not run. Control falls through to `url.c:962`, which sets `m->found = conn` and returns `FALSE` because the NTLM state is idle. `url_match_conn` returns `FALSE` on that, so `url_match_auth_nego`, the only matcher that compares the two origins, never runs, and `url_match_result` at

summary: A request for one origin is sent on a connection that was already authenticated with Negotiate for a different origin, causing credential misuse across origins.

claims.text: A connection authenticated with Negotiate for one origin is reused for a request to a different origin without checking that the new request's credentials match the original authentication context.
claims.reasoning: The code confirms that when a connection is authenticated via Negotiate with Kerberos SSO (no explicit credentials), conn->creds remains NULL while conn->creds_origin is set to the origin. In url_match_auth_ntlm, the else-if branch at line 937 only checks credentials and origin when conn->creds is non-NULL. A subsequent request wanting NTLM (e.g., via --anyauth) passes url_match_auth (Curl_creds_same(NULL,NULL)==TRUE), enters this branch, skips the origin check, sets m->found=conn, and returns FALSE. url_match_conn then returns FALSE so url_match_auth_nego never runs, and the connection gets reused across origins.

claims.text: A request to a second origin behind the same proxy triggers reuse of a connection that was previously authenticated for a different origin because conn->creds remains NULL and the origin check is skipped.
claims.reasoning: The trigger path is confirmed: first request (Negotiate, Kerberos SSO) creates connection with creds_origin=A, creds=NULL. Second request to origin B behind same proxy wants NTLM. url_match_auth passes (NULL==NULL). url_match_auth_ntlm enters line 937 branch, skips origin check (creds=NULL), sets m->found=conn at line 962, returns FALSE. url_match_conn returns FALSE, url_match_auth_nego never runs. Connection reused for origin B.

claims.text: The second host receives the first host's authenticated session and the requesting transfer's own credentials are unused, leading to unauthorized access to the first host's resources.
claims.reasoning: The impact follows from the code path: the second request's credentials (for origin B) are never checked against the connection's authentication context (origin A). The connection authenticated for origin A is used for origin B's request, so origin B sees the authenticated session for origin A. CURLAUTH_ANY includes NTLM, making --anyauth a realistic trigger.

key_reasons: In url_match_auth_ntlm (lib/url.c:937-943), the origin comparison is gated on conn->creds being non-NULL. When a connection is authenticated via Negotiate with Kerberos SSO, conn->creds remains NULL while conn->creds_origin is set (lib/http_negotiate.c@curl-8_21_0:148-149).

A subsequent request wanting NTLM (e.g., --anyauth) passes url_match_auth because Curl_creds_same(NULL,NULL) returns TRUE, enters the gated branch, skips the origin check, marks the connection as a reuse candidate (m->found=conn at line 962), and returns FALSE.

url_match_conn returns FALSE on that FALSE, so url_match_auth_nego (which would compare origins for Negotiate) never runs. The connection pool fallback logic then reuses the connection for the different origin.

This allows a request for origin B to be sent on a connection authenticated for origin A behind a shared proxy, bypassing credential verification. The scenario is realistic for corporate Kerberos SSO deployments.
The flaw exists in both master (ed0338befd1d) and the release curl-8_21_0 (lib/url.c@curl-8_21_0:1014-1020 has the same gated check).
reply: Thank you for the detailed analysis. The flaw is confirmed: in url_match_auth_ntlm (lib/url.c:937-943), the origin check is gated on conn->creds, which stays NULL for Kerberos SSO Negotiate auth (lib/http_negotiate.c:148-149). A later --anyauth request wanting NTLM skips the origin check, marks the connection for reuse, and falls through to reuse it for a different origin behind the same proxy. url_match_auth_nego never runs to catch this. This is a valid cross-origin authentication bypass. We will prepare a fix.
